title: Embedding Cognitive Bias Modification into 3-D Animated Serious Games to Reduce Negative Interpretive Bias and Adverse Mental Health in Early Aged Adolescents with Neurodevelopmental Disorders
content: The difficulties that adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) experience navigating the social nuances of everyday environments make them prone to the cognitive biases that lead to the development of negative thought patterns. Directly tackling the biased interpretive processes that give rise to negative thinking may be effective in reducing mental health problems. Minds Online, a 10-episode 3-D animated serious game embeds cognitive bias modification for interpretation to do this. Using a three-phase multiple baseline design in a school setting, eight adolescents diagnosed with an NDD completed the 10 episodes. Real time data revealed that seven of the eight adolescents altered their negative interpretive bias to a benign bias. Pre- and post-test standardized measures revealed non-significant changes in the desired direction for mental health. Visual analyses of 308 daily self-reported ratings about worry about schoolwork, worry about peer relationships, and feelings of loneliness did not demonstrate a replicated intervention effect. However, when these interrupted time series data were analyzed statistically, significant individual improvements were evident. Engagement with Minds Online was excellent, as was adherence to daily data collection. Minds Online seems to be highly effective in altering the negative interpretive biases of adolescents with NDDs, which is promising because such cognitive biases are involved in the onset and maintenance of psychopathology.
